The `repel-global` scenario with the `secondary` tab renamed to `#secondary`, which disables it: a tab whose name starts with `#` is never a rotation, so it is neither read nor written and its file stays untouched. The `#Global` row `repel primary, secondary` now names a rotation without a tab, so it gets an `error` row above it in `#Global`, is ignored, and is reported on stderr with exit code 1; regeneration still happens because relation errors never block it. Without the constraint `primary` runs plain round robin and produces the same ledger as in `repel-global`. `Notes.csv` has no ledger header and is listed under `ignored` in `#Status` together with `#secondary`; the `tabs` block also shows one rotation, two holidays and one `#Global` row.
